study_identification_part.si4_title: Accommodating Site Variation In Neuroimaging Data Using Normative And Hierarchical Bayesian Models

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Evaluate hierarchical Bayesian normative models that accommodate multi-site scanner effects when modeling age-related cortical thickness, and compare against two-stage harmonization approaches (regress-out, ComBat) for both predictive performance and residual site effects while retaining clinically useful information.

rci3_hc_age.answer: Phase: Uninvestigated | mean: 17.17 | sd: 8.12 | median: NR | iqr: NR | min: 6.5 | max: 40
rci3_hc_age.reason: The paper provides sex-specific age information. Males (n=470): M=17.5, SD=8.3; Females (n=99): M=15.6, SD=7.0; Range: 6.5-40 years. With 470 males and 99 females (569 total), I computed the weighted mean: (17.5*470 + 15.6*99)/569 = 17.17 years. For pooled SD using the standard formula for combining standard deviations: sqrt([(n1-1)*sd1^2 + (n2-1)*sd2^2 + n1*n2/(n1+n2)*(mean1-mean2)^2]/(n1+n2-1)) = sqrt([(469*8.3^2 + 98*7.0^2 + 470*99/569*(17.5-15.6)^2]/568]) ≈ 8.12 years.

nm8_nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The model was validated using a test set (30% of healthy controls, n=166) from the same ABIDE dataset and same 20 sites as the training set (70%, n=389). The split preserved the distribution of age, sex, and site between training and test sets. This represents same-domain, non-independent validation as the data comes from the same acquisition sites with the same scanning protocols, though different individuals. Performance metrics were reported for both training and test sets.
nm8_nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: To evaluate the performance of the models, we split the healthy control data set into a training set (70% of data, n=389) and a test set (30% of data, n=166) using the R package caret and splitstackshape, while the distribution of age, sex and site was preserved between sets. Thus, training and test sets contained individuals from the same sites ('within-site-split')... The normative models were trained on a training set consisting of healthy individuals from the ABIDE data set (70% of the data from 20 different sites, within-site split, preserving the distribution of age and sex across training and test set) and we presented results from generalization to a test set (the remaining 30% of the data from the same sites).
nm8_nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.location: Section 3.3 Model evaluation and comparison; Section 5 Discussion

nm9_nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The model is validated on a held-out test set from the same dataset.
nm9_nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: To evaluate the performance of the models, we split the the healthy control data set into a training set (70% of data, n=389) and a test set (30% of data, n=166) using the R package caret and splitstackshape, while the distribution of age, sex and site was preserved between sets.

nm10_nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: While the paper does not validate on a completely different external dataset from different sites, it does apply the trained normative models to a clinical population (autism sample, n=482) from the same ABIDE dataset but not used in training. This represents a different domain in terms of clinical status (autism vs. healthy controls). The models were validated by comparing deviation patterns between healthy test controls and autism samples, demonstrating retention of clinically useful variance (7-8% atypical in autism vs. 5-6% in controls). However, true external validation on a completely independent dataset from different sites was discussed as future work and is a current limitation.
nm10_nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: In a subsequent step, we applied the hierarchical Bayesian models to 482 individuals with autism from the same data set... Subsequently, we validate the hierarchical Bayesian models in the autism sample of the ABIDE data set and test their ability to retain clinically useful variance while correcting for site effects... The average percentage of atypical z-scores in our study for the autism sample was 7.8% for the HBGPM and 7.2% for the HBLM, compared to 5.7% for the HBGPM and 5.5% for the HBLM for the control test set... the between-site split and the model at its current state only allow generalizations to a test set which includes individuals from the same sites as the training set, thus where the site variation is known.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group comparisons of extreme deviation prevalence (|z|≥1.96) between ASD and control test sets by region; also ANOVA tests to assess residual site effects in z-scores.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Hierarchical Bayesian normative models (HBLM/HBGPM) best captured age-related cortical thickness with minimal residual site effects while preserving clinically informative deviations; two-stage harmonization (regress-out/ComBat) under-scaled predictions and lost >90% variance.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: On the held-out test set, mean ROI-wise correlation was 0.705 (HBGPM) and 0.694 (HBLM), exceeding mod. ComBat (0.568), ComBat (0.343), residuals (0.329) and raw (0.435). Test SRMSE was 0.064 (HBGPM) and 0.066 (HBLM), lower (better) than mod. ComBat (0.075), ComBat (0.085), residuals (0.085) and raw (0.085). MSLL and predicted vs. actual variance plots indicated HBR models retained appropriate variance scaling, whereas harmonization models were poorly scaled (loss >90% of original variance). Forest plots showed substantial site heterogeneity uncorrected, largely removed after HBLM/HBGPM.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Single-stage HBR modeling of site as a random effect provides an alternative to ComBat-style harmonization for normative modeling; comparisons included preserving vs not preserving age/sex variance in ComBat; training/test split preserved site/age/sex distributions.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Validation confined to within-domain ABIDE with within-site split; no external-domain validation; focus limited to cortical thickness (DK atlas) and automated QC; software implementation details not fully specified.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: ABIDE aggregated 20 samples from 17 sites (3T scanners) with varying sequence parameters; site heterogeneity documented (Table 1). Site-specific sample sizes, sex ratios, and age ranges are listed (see Table 1 excerpt). Overall HC age statistics computed from sex-stratified means/SDs and counts.
